/-!
# Conjecture 6.47

by E. I. Khukhro

(C. D. H. Cooper). Let $G$ be a group, $v$ a group word in two variables such that the
operation $x \odot y = v(x, y)$ defines the structure of a new group
$G_v = \langle G, \odot \rangle$ on the set $G$. Does $G_v$ always lie in the variety
generated by $G$?

A group word in two variables is an element $v$ of the free group on two generators, and
$v(x, y)$ is its value under the homomorphism sending the generators to $x$ and $y$.
A word $w$ is a *law* of a group $H$ if every substitution of elements of $H$ for its letters
evaluates $w$ to $1$. The variety generated by $G$ is the class of all groups satisfying every
law of $G$; by Birkhoff's theorem this is the smallest variety containing $G$, i.e. the class of
homomorphic images of subgroups of direct powers of $G$. Hence $G_v$ lies in the variety
generated by $G$ if and only if every law of $G$ is also a law of $G_v$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] {ι : Type*} (w : FreeGroup ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ι → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group word `w` (an element of the free group on the letters `ι`) is a *law* of the
group `G` if every evaluation of `w` in `G` is trivial, i.e. $w(g_i)_i = 1$ for every
assignment $i \mapsto g_i$ of elements of $G$ to the letters.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift (used as the evaluation map); no existing predicate for group laws/identities exists.
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.47».IsLaw
justification.why_needed: Need the notion 'the word w is a law (identity) of the group G', i.e. every evaluation FreeGroup.lift f w equals 1. Not present in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (searched for variety/law/identity in GroupTheory and the helper library).

blocks.name: IsLaw
blocks.text:
/-- A group word `w` (an element of the free group on the letters `ι`) is a *law* of the
group `G` if every evaluation of `w` in `G` is trivial, i.e. $w(g_i)_i = 1$ for every
assignment $i \mapsto g_i$ of elements of $G$ to the letters. -/
def IsLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] {ι : Type*} (w : FreeGroup ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ι → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

blocks.code:
def MemVarietyGeneratedBy (H : Type*) [Group H] (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w : FreeGroup ℕ, IsLaw G w → IsLaw H w
blocks.docstring:
The group `H` lies in the variety generated by the group `G` if every law of `G` is
also a law of `H`. Laws are taken in countably many letters, which covers all group words
since each involves only finitely many letters.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib; the only 'variety' hits are algebraic geometry. Considered defining HSP(G) directly, but the equational (laws) definition is the standard one and far simpler.
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.47».MemVarietyGeneratedBy
justification.why_needed: Need 'H lies in the variety generated by G'. Formalized as: every law of G in countably many variables (FreeGroup ℕ) is a law of H, which by Birkhoff's theorem is equivalent to H ∈ HSP(G). Mathlib has no notion of varieties of groups.

blocks.name: MemVarietyGeneratedBy
blocks.text:
/-- The group `H` lies in the variety generated by the group `G` if every law of `G` is
also a law of `H`. Laws are taken in countably many letters, which covers all group words
since each involves only finitely many letters. -/
def MemVarietyGeneratedBy (H : Type*) [Group H] (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w : FreeGroup ℕ, IsLaw G w → IsLaw H w

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.47» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [hG : Group G] (v : FreeGroup (Fin 2)) (hv : Group G),
      (∀ x y : G, hv.mul x y = @FreeGroup.lift _ G hG ![x, y] v) →
      @MemVarietyGeneratedBy G hv G hG := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
(C. D. H. Cooper). Let $G$ be a group, $v$ a group word in two variables such that the
operation $x \odot y = v(x, y)$ defines the structure of a new group
$G_v = \langle G, \odot \rangle$ on the set $G$. Does $G_v$ always lie in the variety
generated by $G$?

Here `hG` is the given group structure on `G`, `v : FreeGroup (Fin 2)` is the word in the
variables `FreeGroup.of 0` and `FreeGroup.of 1`, whose value $v(x, y)$ computed in the original
group `(G, hG)` is `@FreeGroup.lift _ G hG ![x, y] v`, and `hv` is a group structure on the same
type `G` whose multiplication is $x \odot y = v(x, y)$; the group $G_v$ is `G` with the structure
`hv`. Since a group structure is determined by its multiplication, quantifying over all such `hv`
is the same as assuming that $\odot$ is a group operation. The instance `hG` is passed explicitly
because `hv` is also a local instance on `G`.

theorem isMulCommutative_iff_isLaw_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMulCommutative G ↔ IsLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2), FreeGroup.of (1 : Fin 2)⁆ := by
  constructor
  · intro _ f
    simp [commutatorElement_def, mul_comm]
  · intro h
    refine ⟨⟨fun x y => ?_⟩⟩
    simpa [commutatorElement_def, mul_inv_eq_one, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul] using h ![x, y]

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with implicit universal quantification over all groups G and all two-variable group words v (elements of the free group on two generators, evaluated in G) such that the binary operation (x,y) ↦ v(x,y) on the underlying set of G satisfies the group axioms; 'G_v lies in the variety generated by G' means every law (identity) holding in G also holds in G_v, i.e. G_v ∈ var(G) in the Birkhoff sense, so the Prop is 'answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G v, (v defines a group structure on G) → G_v satisfies all laws of G'.
claims.reviewer_why: c03's design (bespoke `IsLaw` over an arbitrary letter type and `MemVarietyGeneratedBy H G` := every law of G is a law of H; G_v modelled as a second `Group G` structure `hv` with `hv.mul x y = v(x,y)` evaluated in the ORIGINAL structure via `@FreeGroup.lift _ G hG`) is faithful and readable. Verified with pp.explicit that `hG` is used for evaluating v and for the source laws, and `hv` only for ⊙ and the target laws; verified by `Iff.rfl` that the conclusion unfolds to `∀ w : FreeGroup ℕ, (∀ f, lift_hG f w = 1) → ∀ f, lift_hv f w = 1`. answer(True) = 'yes, G_v always lies in var(G)'. Follows the Kourovka-directory convention `∀ (G : Type) [Group G] ...`. I added c02's API lemmas (commutator law ↔ commutative, x^n law ↔ exponent divides n) and tightened the docstring. c01, c02, c06, c07 were also faithful (equivalent encodings via FreeGroup ℕ or ∀ n, FreeGroup (Fin n)); c04 faithful but clunkier (letI-based helper defs).

/-!
# Conjecture 6.47

by E. I. Khukhro

(C. D. H. Cooper). Let $G$ be a group, $v$ a group word in two variables such that the
operation $x \odot y = v(x, y)$ defines the structure of a new group
$G_v = \langle G, \odot \rangle$ on the set $G$. Does $G_v$ always lie in the variety

generated by $G$ if and only if every law of $G$ is also a law of $G_v$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.47»

/-- A group word `w` (an element of the free group on the letters `ι`) is a *law* of the
group `G` if every evaluation of `w` in `G` is trivial, i.e. $w(g_i)_i = 1$ for every
assignment $i \mapsto g_i$ of elements of $G$ to the letters. -/
def IsLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] {ι : Type*} (w : FreeGroup ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ι → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- The group `H` lies in the variety generated by the group `G` if every law of `G` is
also a law of `H`. Laws are taken in countably many letters, which covers all group words
since each involves only finitely many letters. -/
def MemVarietyGeneratedBy (H : Type*) [Group H] (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w : FreeGroup ℕ, IsLaw G w → IsLaw H w

/--
(C. D. H. Cooper). Let $G$ be a group, $v$ a group word in two variables such that the
operation $x \odot y = v(x, y)$ defines the structure of a new group
$G_v = \langle G, \odot \rangle$ on the set $G$. Does $G_v$ always lie in the variety
generated by $G$?

Here `hG` is the given group structure on `G`, `v : FreeGroup (Fin 2)` is the word in the
variables `FreeGroup.of 0` and `FreeGroup.of 1`, whose value $v(x, y)$ computed in the original
group `(G, hG)` is `@FreeGroup.lift _ G hG ![x, y] v`, and `hv` is a group structure on the same
type `G` whose multiplication is $x \odot y = v(x, y)$; the group $G_v$ is `G` with the structure
`hv`. Since a group structure is determined by its multiplication, quantifying over all such `hv`
is the same as assuming that $\odot$ is a group operation. The instance `hG` is passed explicitly
because `hv` is also a local instance on `G`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.47» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [hG : Group G] (v : FreeGroup (Fin 2)) (hv : Group G),
      (∀ x y : G, hv.mul x y = @FreeGroup.lift _ G hG ![x, y] v) →
      @MemVarietyGeneratedBy G hv G hG := by
  sorry

/-- Every group lies in the variety it generates. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem memVarietyGeneratedBy_self (G : Type*) [Group G] : MemVarietyGeneratedBy G G :=
  fun _ h => h

/-- The trivial word is a law of every group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_one (G : Type*) [Group G] {ι : Type*} : IsLaw G (1 : FreeGroup ι) :=
  fun _ => map_one _

/-- The commutator word $[x_0, x_1]$ is a law of $G$ if and only if $G$ is commutative. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMulCommutative_iff_isLaw_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMulCommutative G ↔ IsLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2), FreeGroup.of (1 : Fin 2)⁆ := by
  constructor
  · intro _ f
    simp [commutatorElement_def, mul_comm]
  · intro h
    refine ⟨⟨fun x y => ?_⟩⟩
    simpa [commutatorElement_def, mul_inv_eq_one, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul] using h ![x, y]

/-- The word $x_0^n$ is a law of $G$ if and only if every element of $G$ satisfies $x^n = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_of_pow_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] (n : ℕ) :
    IsLaw G (FreeGroup.of () ^ n) ↔ ∀ x : G, x ^ n = 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h x
    simpa using h fun _ => x
  · intro h f
    simp [h]

/-- The word $v = x_0 x_1$ defines the original multiplication of `G`, so the original group
structure satisfies the hypothesis of `kourovka.«6.47»`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mul_eq_lift_of_mul_of (G : Type*) [Group G] (x y : G) :
    x * y = FreeGroup.lift ![x, y] (FreeGroup.of 0 * FreeGroup.of 1) := by
  simp

end Kourovka.«6.47»

items: G_v is modeled literally as a second Group structure `hv` on the same type `G`, with the compatibility hypothesis `hv.mul x y = v(x,y)`; since identity and inverses are determined by the multiplication, universally quantifying over all such `hv` is equivalent to 'if ⊙ is a group operation then G_v ∈ var(G)'. A reviewer may prefer the alternative of a separate type `Gv` with a bijection `e : G ≃ Gv` transporting ⊙; the two are equivalent since variety membership is isomorphism-invariant.

Because every binder of class type is a local instance in Lean 4, the more recent `hv` shadows `hG`. The evaluation of v is therefore written `@FreeGroup.lift _ G hG ![x, y] v` so that v(x,y) is computed in the ORIGINAL group (verified with pp.explicit; without the explicit `hG` Lean used `hv`, which would be wrong). The conclusion is `@MemVarietyGeneratedBy G hv G hG`, i.e. laws of (G,hG) hold in (G,hv); verified by unfolding to `∀ w, (∀ f, @FreeGroup.lift ℕ G hG f w = hG.one) → ∀ f, @FreeGroup.lift ℕ G hv f w = hv.one`.
Two-variable words are elements of `FreeGroup (Fin 2)` (this includes words using only one or neither variable, as is standard); v(x,y) = FreeGroup.lift ![x, y] v.

Laws are taken in `FreeGroup ℕ` (countably many variables). Every group word uses finitely many variables, so this captures all laws; a variety generated by G is the class of groups satisfying all laws of G (Birkhoff).
The word 'new' in 'a new group G_v' is read as merely descriptive, not as requiring G_v ≠ G; the quantification is over all v that define a group operation (including v = x y).
Quantification is over `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files in the repository.

Added short, fully proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions (reflexivity of MemVarietyGeneratedBy, trivial word is a law, commutator word is a law of commutative groups, and that v = x₀x₁ recovers the original multiplication, showing the hypothesis is satisfiable).

reviewer_notes: Faithfulness checks: (1) 'group word in two variables' = FreeGroup (Fin 2), evaluated via FreeGroup.lift ![x, y] (0 ↦ x, 1 ↦ y; checked by rfl). (2) 'defines a group structure on the set G' = universal quantification over a second `Group G` structure whose `mul` is v(x,y); since Mathlib's Group structure (one, inv, div, npow, zpow) is propositionally determined by mul, this equals '(∃ group structure with this multiplication) → ...'. (3) 'lies in the variety generated by G' = every law of G is a law of G_v (Birkhoff), as the decomposition notes direct. (4) G : Type (universe 0) follows the existing Kourovka files. Rejected candidates: c08 is trivially true — instance shadowing makes `wordEval v x y` and `@MemVarietyGenerated G G _ Gv` elaborate with `Gv` in BOTH positions (confirmed by pp.explicit: `MemVarietyGenerated G G Gv Gv`), so its conclusion says G_v lies in its own variety. c05 quantifies the assignment `f` before the law hypothesis (`∀ n w₁ w₂ f, w₁(f)=w₂(f) in G → w₁(f)=w₂(f) in G_v`), a pointwise condition far stronger than law preservation, and also uses a `let` binder in the statement. No candidate omitted the slot; no decomposition objections were raised. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; all lines ≤ 100 chars.
